rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura commands the Prophet to pray at night to prepare for the weighty revelation, endure opponents' abuse, and leave them graciously; it warns unbelievers, extends the ruling to believers, then eases it.
rows.anchor: تأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بقيام الليل والصلاة فيه ليستعد بذلك لتلقي ثقل ما سيلقى عليه من القول الثقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura is Meccan and among the earliest revelations; it is said to be the second or third sura revealed.
rows.anchor: والسورة مكية من عتائق السور النازلة في أول البعثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muzzammil is the active participle of tazammul, wrapping oneself in cloth for sleep or similar purposes.
rows.anchor: أصله المتزمل اسم فاعل من التزمل بمعنى التلفف بالثوب لنوم ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is neither disparaging nor complimentary, despite what some have supposed.
rows.anchor: وليس في الخطاب به تهجين ولا تحسين كما توهمه بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context suggests the Prophet was mocked and hurt in his mission, grieved for God, and wrapped himself to sleep and escape distress.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يستفاد من سياق الآيات أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان قد قوبل في دعوته بالهزء والسخرية والإيذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in 2:45, prayer and patience are means to resist severe distress; the Prophet is directed to them instead of wrapping himself up to sleep.
rows.anchor: فأفيد بذلك أن عليه أن يقاوم الكرب العظام والنوائب المرة بالصلاة والصبر لا بالتزمل والنوم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes al-muzzammil as the bearer of the burdens of the mantle of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد يا أيها المتزمل بعباءة النبوة أي المتحمل لأثقالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mantle-of-prophethood interpretation has no support in the wording.
rows.anchor: ولا شاهد عليه من جهة اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Standing the night means rising during it for prayer; al-layl functions as an object by broad usage, as in saying one entered the house.
rows.anchor: المراد بقيام الليل القيام فيه إلى الصلاة فالليل مفعول به توسعا كما في قولهم دخلت الدار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing supplies an implied destination after qom and makes al-layl an adverb: rise for prayer at night.
rows.anchor: والتقدير قم إلى الصلاة في الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception illa qalilan is taken from the night.
rows.anchor: وقوله { إلا قليلا } استثناء من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred parsing makes half a substitute for the night-except-a-little phrase; its pronouns refer to the half and night, offering a choice of half, slightly less, or slightly more.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أنه بدل من { الليل إلا قليلا } المتعلق به تكليف القيام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative makes half a substitute for the excepted little: stand all but half, or a little more or less than half.
rows.anchor: وقيل { نصفه } بدل من المستثنى أعني { قليلا } فيكون المعنى قم الليل إلا نصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though both parsings yield the same result, the first comes sooner to mind because clarifying the ruling's object precedes clarifying its attached details.
rows.anchor: والوجهان وإن اتحدا في النتيجة غير أن الوجه السابق أسبق إلى الذهن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One parsing makes half a substitute for the night and understands the exception as a few excused nights, such as nights of illness or overpowering sleep.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن نصفه بدل من الليل لكن المراد بالقليل القليل من الليالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This excused-nights reading is possible, but the earlier reading is more immediately apparent.
rows.anchor: ولا بأس بهذا الوجه لكن الوجه الأول أسبق منه إلى الذهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tartil is reciting the Quran while distinctly articulating its letters in sequence.
rows.anchor: ترتيل القرآن تلاوته بتبيين حروفه على تواليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tartil clause coordinates with the command to stand: stand at night and recite the Quran distinctly.
rows.anchor: أي قم الليل واقرأ القرآن بترتيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparently tartil means reciting in the night prayer, or refers to the prayer itself.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد بترتيل القرآن ترتيله في الصلاة أو المراد به الصلاة نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran calls prayer by a similar expression in 17:78, including the witnessed dawn recitation.
rows.anchor: عبر سبحانه عن الصلاة بنظير هذا التعبير في قوله أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view reads the command as requiring Quran recitation without prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد إيجاب قراءة القرآن دون الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Physical heaviness is figuratively applied to meanings that are difficult for the soul to bear, grasp, tolerate, realize, or practice persistently.
rows.anchor: الثقل كيفية جسمانية من خاصته أنه يشق حمل الجسم الثقيل ونقله من مكان إلى مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A saying can be called heavy when it is hard to understand or tolerate, such as subtle scholarship offered to ordinary minds.
rows.anchor: فربما أضيف إلى القول من جهة معناه فعد ثقيلا لتضمنه معنى يشق على النفس إدراكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is heavy because it contains truths difficult to realize and duties difficult to perform and maintain.
rows.anchor: أو لتضمنه حقائق يصعب التحقق بها أو تكاليف يشق الاتيان بها والمداومة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As divine speech from the realm of majesty, the Quran's meaning can only be received by a purified soul detached from all but God; it has outer and inner senses, revelation and interpretation, and explains everything.
rows.anchor: القرآن قول إلهي ثقيل بكلا المعنيين أما من حيث تلقي معناه فإنه كلام إلهي مأخوذ من ساحة العظمة والكبرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is also heavy in realizing the reality of monotheism and its related beliefs.
rows.anchor: وأما من حيث التحقق بحقيقة التوحيد وما يتبعها من الحقائق الاعتقادية فكفى في الاشارة إلى ثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's weight was evident in the Prophet's bouts of distress and near-fainting, as reported in numerous traditions.
rows.anchor: وقد كان ثقله مشهودا من حال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بما كان يأخذه من البرحاء وشبه الإغماء على ما وردت به الأخبار المستفيضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nashi'at may be a verbal noun like al-aqibah and al-afiyah, meaning arising or coming into being, or an active participle attached to an omitted noun.
rows.anchor: الناشئة أما مصدر كالعاقبة والعافية بمعنى النشأة وهي الحدوث والتكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either derivation, the phrase refers to the night; another reported view takes it as night prayer.
rows.anchor: وكيف كان فالمراد بها الليل وإطلاق الحادثة على الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Footfall on the earth is a metaphor for firmer footing, since the soul is clear of daytime distractions.
rows.anchor: وكونها أشد وطأ كناية عن كونها أثبت قدما لصفاء النفس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as the heart agreeing with the tongue.
rows.anchor: وقيل الوطء مواطاة القلب اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with a long alif, أشد وطاء, supports interpreting the phrase as heart-tongue concord.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكونها أقوم قيلا كونها أثبت قولا وأصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night speech is more stable and correct because the heart is present and voices are quiet.
rows.anchor: كونها أثبت قولا وأصوب لحضور القلب وهدو الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night, or prayer in it, provides firmer footing and speech because God made night a repose, cutting off livelihood distractions and freeing the mind.
rows.anchor: لما أن الله جعل الليل سكنا يستتبع انقطاع الإنسان عن شواغل المعيشة إلى نفسه وفراغ باله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sabhan means swimming swiftly in water; a long swim by day figuratively describes immersion in livelihood concerns and varied errands.
rows.anchor: السبح المشي السريع في الماء والسبح الطويل في النهار كناية عن الغور في مهمات المعاش

words: إن لك في النهار سبحا طويلا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is filled with many consuming occupations, leaving no free time for complete orientation toward God; therefore the Prophet should pray at night.
rows.anchor: إن لك في النهار مشاغل كثيرة تشتغل بها مستوعبة لا تدع لك فراغا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says daytime affords time to sleep, manage livelihood, and attend to needs, leaving the night for vigil.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن لك في النهار فراغا لنومك وتدبير أمر معاشك والتصرف في حوائجك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view says missed night worship can be made up in the day, as in 25:62.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى إن لك في النهار فراغا فإن فاتك من الليل شيء أمكنك أن تتداركه في النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation of daytime as consuming work best fits the context; the make-up interpretation is linked to 25:62.
rows.anchor: والذي قدمناه من المعنى أنسب للمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commands to remember God and devote oneself to Him describe night prayer and explain the command to recite with tartil.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنه يصف صلاة الليل فهو كالعطف التفسيري على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, remembering the Lord's name is verbal remembrance accompanied by the heart, and devotion likewise includes verbal expression.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد بذكر اسم الرب تعالى الذكر اللفظي بمواطاة من القلب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative generalizes the command to continuous customary remembrance day and night in any form, since the Prophet never forgot God.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية تعميم بعد التخصيص والمراد بالذكر دوام ذكره تعالى ليلا ونهارا على أي وجه كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not forgetting God does not rule out a command to remember Him verbally; not forgetting before an address does not rule out a later command.
rows.anchor: أن عدم نسيانه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ربه إلى حين الخطاب لا ينافي أمره بذكره بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that perpetual remembrance is impossible or merely customary: God is never absent from a person, whether noticed or overlooked.
rows.anchor: فالله جل ذكره مذكور للإنسان لا يغيب عنه ولا لحظه سواء تنبه عليه الإنسان أو غفل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may make Himself known so that a person never loses awareness of Him; this state is not exclusive to angels, as 41:38 and 21:20 show.
rows.anchor: ومن الممكن أن يعرفه الله نفسه بحيث لا يغفل عنه ولا في حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name may mean one of God's names or specifically the name Allah.
rows.anchor: أمر بذكر اسم من أسمائه أو لفظ الجلالة خاصة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the name as the basmala.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به البسملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from first-person plural to third person may awaken awareness of servitude, the bond between servant and Lord.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله { ربك } التفات عن التكلم مع الغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabattul means turning away from others and devoting oneself to God.
rows.anchor: فسر التبتل بالانقطاع أي وانقطع إلى الله

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: A report from the Imams of the Prophet's family explains tabattul as raising one's hands to God and beseeching Him; al-Tabataba'i finds this fitting if remembrance is verbal.
rows.anchor: ومن المروي عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن التبتل رفع اليد إلى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabtil is an absolute object where the expected verbal noun would be tabattul.
rows.anchor: مفعول مطلق ظاهرا وكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال وتبتل إليه تبتلا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says tabattul carries the sense of batala: sever yourself completely from everything but God, or compel yourself to raise your hands and plead.
rows.anchor: قيل لتضمين تبتل معنى بتل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A different explanation says the form was chosen to preserve the verse endings.
rows.anchor: وقيل لمراعاة الفواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is detached from its adjectival role, with an implied huwa: He is Lord of east and west.
rows.anchor: وصف مقطوع عن الوصفية والتقدير هو رب المشرق والمغرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: East and west are relative directions encompassing the whole observable world; they are named in connection with the preceding night and day and their rising and setting.
rows.anchor: فإن المشرق والمغرب جهتان نسبيتان تشملان جهات العالم المشهود كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God Lord of the whole world prevents taking Him as the Prophet's private deity, like a pagan's personal idol, and grounds the call to monotheism.
rows.anchor: مأمور باتخاذه ربا لأنه ربه ورب العالم كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusive divinity follows from exclusive lordship: worship is a branch of lordship as ownership and governance, so He alone is God because He alone is Lord.
rows.anchor: فإن الالوهية وهي المعبودية من فروع الربوبية التي هي الملك والتدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking God as trustee applies to all affairs; appointing a trustee means making another's will and acts stand in place of one's own.
rows.anchor: وتوكيل الوكيل هو إقامة الانسان غيره مقام نفسه بحيث تقوم إرادته مقام إرادته وعمله مقام عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly events, trust means denying independent efficacy to apparent causes while still using the means God taught, and attributing success to God's choice.
rows.anchor: فلا مؤثر في الوجود بحقيقة معنى التأثير إلا الله فلا يتعلق بتأثير سبب من الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse eases the earlier night-prayer command by allowing what is manageable from the Quran, without abrogating the original instruction to stand the specified portions.
rows.anchor: ولسان الآية هو التخفيف بما تيسر من القرآن من غير نسخ لأصل الحكم السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports place this Meccan verse eight months, a year, or ten years after the sura's opening verses.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في غير واحد من الأخبار أن الآية مكية نزلت بعد ثمانية أشهر أو سنة أو عشر سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer followed by obligatory zakat and distinguished from voluntary charity suggests zakat here is obligatory, which was instituted in Medina after the Hijra.
rows.anchor: وإنما فرضت الزكاة بالمدينة بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say zakat was imposed in Mecca without specified thresholds, while Medina later specified its thresholds.
rows.anchor: وقول بعضهم إن الزكاة فرضت بمكة من غير تعيين الأنصباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that Meccan zakat was imposed without specifying thresholds is unsupported.
rows.anchor: تحكم من غير دليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some propose that the verse was revealed earlier but its legal ruling took effect later; the author calls this unsupported.
rows.anchor: قول بعضهم إنه من الممكن أن تكون الآية مما تأخر حكمه عن نزوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed-ruling proposal is also conjecture without evidence.
rows.anchor: تحكم من غير دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning fighting would not suit the early mission's circumstances, so the verse is apparently Medinan; some others also favor this dating.
rows.anchor: فالظاهر أن الآية مدنية وليست بمكية وقد مال إليه بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing God as your Lord intimates divine mercy and care; noting that He knows the Prophet's vigil also suggests gratitude for his effort, as in 17:19.
rows.anchor: تلويح إلى شمول الرحمة والعناية الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adna is a comparative from nearness, conventionally meaning just less than an amount: a count near ten is nine, not eleven.
rows.anchor: وقد جرى العرف على استعمال أدنى فيما يقرب من الشيء وهو أقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw is additive: on some nights the Prophet stands just under two-thirds, on others half, and on others a third.
rows.anchor: لمطلق الجمع والمراد أنه يعلم أنك تقوم في بعض الليالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with the Prophet means his fellow believers, and min is partitive; some of them also kept night vigil.
rows.anchor: فالآية تدل على أن بعضهم كان يقوم الليل كما كان يقومه النبي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing takes min as explanatory; the author dismisses this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل { من } بيانية، وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows because He is the creator and determiner; determining night and day entails determining their thirds, halves, and two-thirds.
rows.anchor: في مقام التعليل لقوله { إن ربك يعلم } والمعنى وكيف لا يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names Allah in connection with measurement because determining measures is a matter of creation, and all creation belongs to Him.
rows.anchor: لأن التقدير من شؤون الخلق والخلق إلى الله الذي إليه ينتهي كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihsa means obtaining a measure or number and encompassing the thing.
rows.anchor: الاحصاء تحصيل مقدار الشيء وعدده والإحاطة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in lan tuhsuhu may refer to measuring night or to standing for its prescribed thirds, half, or near two-thirds.
rows.anchor: وضمير { لن تحصوه } للتقدير أو للقيام مقدار ثلث الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calculating fixed portions through nights of changing annual length is hard for ordinary people, especially those sleeping early without staying awake all night to be certain.
rows.anchor: وإحصاء ذلك مع اختلاف الليالي طولا وقصرا في أيام السنة مما لا يتيسر لعامة المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knew that the prescribed night amount could not be calculated with ease by the generality of those obligated.
rows.anchor: علمه تعالى بعدم تيسر إحصاء المقدار الذي أمروا بقيامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here God's tawba toward people means His merciful turning to them through easing the burden.
rows.anchor: توبته تعالى ورجوعه إليهم بمعنى انعطاف الرحمة الإلهية عليهم بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's turning in mercy can enable repentance or obedience, lift some duties, or ease them; 9:118 describes Him turning to people so that they might repent.
rows.anchor: فلله سبحانه توبة على عباده ببسط رحمته عليهم وأثرها توفيقهم للتوبة أو لمطلق الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A distinct usage is God's return to people after their repentance, whose effect is forgiveness of their sins.
rows.anchor: كما أن له توبة عليهم بمعنى الرجوع إليهم بعد توبتهم وأثرها مغفرة ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command eases the amount of night vigil for the generality of believers because they cannot calculate the specified portions; it does not cancel the original rule for those able to keep it.
rows.anchor: التخفيف في قيام الليل من حيث المقدار لعامة المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The difficulty applies to the obligated group collectively, not every person: the Prophet and some companions could keep the portions, so others receive a concession while the original option remains.
rows.anchor: إنما لا يتيسر لمجموع المكلفين لا لجميعهم ولو امتنع لجميعهم ولم يتيسر لأحدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night vigil is recommended for other believers, although the address to the Prophet appears obligatory.
rows.anchor: والحكم استحبابي لسائر المؤمنين وإن كان ظاهر ما للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من الخطاب الوجوب

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: Commentators disagree whether the original night command meant prayer or Quran recitation outside prayer.
rows.anchor: وللقوم في كون المراد بقيام الليل الصلاة فيه أو قراءة القرآن خارج الصلاة

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: One reported legal view makes night vigil obligatory for both the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: في كونه واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: Another reported view recommends night vigil for everyone.
rows.anchor: أو مستحبا للجميع

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: A third view makes it obligatory for the Prophet and recommended for others.
rows.anchor: أو واجبا على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم مستحبا لغيره

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: Commentators also disagree whether the easing abrogated the earlier ruling or changed the commanded prayer into reciting what is manageable.
rows.anchor: ثم في نسخ الحكم بالتخفيف بما تيسر بهذه الآية أو تبديل الصلاة من قراءة ما تيسر من القرآن أقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness, travel, and fighting provide another reason for easing exact night portions, since calculating them is especially difficult in those circumstances.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى مصلحة أخرى مقتضية للتخفيف في أمر القيام ثلث الليل أو نصفه

words: وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Traveling in search of God's bounty means journeying between lands for livelihood through trade.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالضرب في الأرض للابتغاء من فضل الله طلب الرزق بالمسافرة من أرض إلى أرض للتجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated concession to recite what is manageable reinforces the easing.
rows.anchor: وقوله { فاقرءوا ما تيسر منه وأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة وأقرضوا الله قرضا حسنا } تكرار للتخفيف تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in minhu refers to the Quran.
rows.anchor: وضمير { منه } للقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer should be performed in a way suited to the amount of time spent standing.
rows.anchor: والمراد الإتيان بالصلاة على ما يناسب سعة الوقت الذي قاموا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer to be established is obligatory: if the verse is Medinan, it is the five daily prayers; if Meccan, it is whatever prayers were then prescribed.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالصلاة المأمور بإقامتها الفريضة فإن كانت الآية مدنية فالفرائض الخمس اليومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The zakat commanded is obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالزكاة الزكاة المفروضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lending God a good loan means financial donations in His cause beyond obligatory zakat.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإقراضه تعالى غير الزكاة من الإنفاقات المالية في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pairing prayer, zakat, and charity signals that religious duties remain in force; the easing does not spread to every obligation, as in 58:13.
rows.anchor: وعطف الأمر بإقامة الصلاة وإيتاء الزكاة والإقراض للتلويح إلى أن التكاليف الدينية على حالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min khayr explains the relative pronoun, and khayr means all obedience, obligatory and recommended.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالخير مطلق الطاعة أعم من الواجبة والمندوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huwa is either a separator pronoun or an emphatic repetition of the object pronoun in tajiduhu.
rows.anchor: أو تأكيد للضمير في { تجدوه }

words: وما تقدموا لأنفسكم من خير تجدوه عند الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience sent ahead for the afterlife is found with God on the day of meeting, better than anything done or left undone and greater in reward.
rows.anchor: خيرا من كل ما تعملون أو تتركون وأعظم أجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing command is to seek God's forgiveness; His description as forgiving and merciful intimates a promise of pardon and mercy.
rows.anchor: وقوله { واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور رحيم } ختم الكلام بالأمر بالاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows that seeking forgiveness may mean performing all acts of obedience, since they are means to God's forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ولا يبعد أن يكون المراد بالاستغفار الإتيان بمطلق الطاعات لأنها وسائل يتوسل بها إلى مغفرة الله

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far's report says the Prophet observed and announced the night vigil, people struggled to calculate the portions and sometimes stayed until dawn fearing error, and God eased it; it adds that every prophet prayed at night, never beginning early in the evening.
rows.anchor: في تفسير القمي في رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abu Ja'far report presents the sura's opening as requiring night prayer and its ending as abrogating that duty; al-Tabataba'i says his preceding discussion addresses this view.
rows.anchor: أقول محصل الرواية أن صدر السورة توجب صلاة الليل وذيلها تنسخها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Similar reports through Sunni routes from Ibn Abbas and others also describe abrogation of the opening night-prayer command.
rows.anchor: وروي ما يقرب منه من طرق أهل السنة عن ابن عباس وغيره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report cited by al-Majma through al-Haskani, al-Kalbi, and Abu Salih, identifies the accompanying group as Ali and Abu Dharr.
rows.anchor: روى الحاكم أبو القاسم إبراهيم الحسكاني بإسناده عن الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الرضا عن أبيه عن جده
rows.claim: A report from al-Rida, his father, and his grandfather says what is easy to recite is what brings humility of heart and purity of the inner self.
rows.anchor: روي عن الرضا عن أبيه عن جده عليهم السلام قال ما تيسر منه لكم فيه خشوع القلب

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet explained what is easy as one hundred verses.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم والطبراني وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس عن النبي

words: وآخرون يضربون في الأرض يبتغون من فضل الله
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports Ibn Masud quoting the Prophet: a trader who imports food to a Muslim town and sells at the day's price has the rank of a martyr; the Prophet then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وفيه أخرج ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: سماعة
rows.claim: In al-Qummi's tafsir, Zur'ah transmits Sama'ah's answer that a goodly loan is something other than zakat.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي بإسناده عن زرعة عن سماعة قال سألته عن قول الله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali's hadith of the four hundred advises frequent seeking of forgiveness to attract provision and advancing whatever good one can; its final phrase derives from 73:20.
rows.anchor: وفي الخصال عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في حديث الأربعمائة أكثروا الاستغفار تجلبوا الرزق

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Some take the omitted object of the preceding command to warn as all people, citing 34:28.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلناك إلا كافة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura does not pair warning with glad tidings because it came at the beginning of the mission, when warning predominated.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر التبشير مع الإنذار مع أنهما كالمتلازمين في تمام الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Magnify the Lord inwardly and outwardly, in belief, deed, speech, and action: nothing equals, surpasses, resists, diminishes, or bounds Him.
rows.anchor: أي أنسب ربك إلى الكبرياء والعظمة اعتقادا وعملا قولا وفعلا

rows.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
rows.claim: The Imams of the Prophet's family explain takbir as declaring God too great to be described, even by the descriptions used of Him.
rows.anchor: ولذا ورد عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن معنى التكبير الله أكبر من أن يوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takbir expresses the Islamic monotheism that surpasses other revealed traditions: God exceeds every description, including the description of being greater.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو المناسب للتوحيد الإسلامي الذي يفوق ما نجده من معنى التوحيد في سائر الشرائع السماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih negates deficient, privative attributes such as death, incapacity, and ignorance; Allahu akbar is absolute transcendence of every positive or negative description.
rows.anchor: فسبحان الله تنزيه له تعالى عن كل وصف عدمي مبني على النقص كالموت والعجز والجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every concept is bounded and limited to itself, while God cannot be encompassed by a limit.
rows.anchor: كل مفهوم محدود في نفسه لا يتعدى إلى غيره من المفاهيم وهو تعالى لا يحيط به حد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the command as saying takbir in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد الأمر بالتكبير في الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Him your Lord subtly suggests that His oneness was then particular to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عنه تعالى بربك لا يخلو من إشعار بأن توحيده تعالى يومئذ كان يختص به

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the fa as conditional: whatever the situation, do not neglect magnifying God.
rows.anchor: ودخلت الفاء لمعنى الشرط كأنه قيل وما كان فلا تدع تكبيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation makes clean clothes a metaphor for sound deeds: action clothes the soul and manifests its beliefs, and clean garments often stand for good conduct.
rows.anchor: قيل كناية عن إصلاح العمل ولا يخلو من وجه فإن العمل بمنزلة الثياب للنفس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the command as purifying the soul from sins and disobedience.
rows.anchor: وقيل كناية عن تزكية النفس وتنزيهها عن الذنوب والمعاصي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view commands shortening garments so they will not drag on the ground and become impure.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد تقصير الثياب لأنه أبعد من النجاسة ولو طالت وانجرت على الأرض

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes the garments as the Prophet's wives and commands purifying them from disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد تطهير الأزواج من الكفر والمعاصي
